story.title: Democrat Haley Stevens Endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate Race
story.summary: Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate in Michigan, a move that has drawn criticism from her party. This endorsement comes just two days before the midterm elections and follows a public feud between Stevens and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed over campaign ads. Stevens' decision is seen as a significant blow to El-Sayed's campaign.

event_overview.title: About Michigan Senate Race
event_overview.subject: Michigan Senate Race
event_overview.summary: The Michigan Senate race is the statewide 2026 election for one U.S. Senate seat representing Michigan. Voters are choosing a senator for a six-year term in the November 3, 2026 general election; the official ballot lists Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, Republican nominee Mike Rogers, and candidates from four additional parties.

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: The Michigan Department of State and its Bureau of Elections publish the official candidate listings, voter information, and election results resources for the statewide election.

facts.label: Primary context
facts.value: Michigan held its 2026 primary on August 4 before the November general election.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the November 1-2, 2026 endorsement-related developments involving Haley Stevens, Mike Rogers, and Abdul El-Sayed, not the race’s full campaign, all ballot candidates, voting process, or final results.

explore_lenses.label: What prompted Stevens’s reversal?
explore_lenses.title: A dispute over campaign boundaries and rhetoric
explore_lenses.summary: Stevens’s switch followed a breakdown in a planned display of post-primary unity with El-Sayed. The immediate flashpoint was an outside group’s Israel-related ad and the El-Sayed campaign’s request that Stevens stay away from its remaining events.

claims.text: ABC reported that Stevens said El-Sayed had told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign; she cited that exclusion when announcing her endorsement of Rogers.
The disputed grocery-price ad was made by Rebellion PAC, not El-Sayed’s campaign; his campaign said it was not affiliated with the ad, and El-Sayed said he did not agree with its contents.
Stevens characterized the ad as antisemitic and had pressed El-Sayed to condemn it; El-Sayed’s campaign framed Stevens’s criticism as an effort to reopen their August primary contest.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the Senate race?
explore_lenses.title: Voting, then Michigan’s canvass timetable
explore_lenses.summary: The endorsement does not alter the certified general-election nominees; voters decide the race on November 3. Michigan’s formal canvass deadlines then govern when statewide results are reviewed and certified.

claims.text: Michigan’s Board of State Canvassers certified the August primary nominees, including the candidates qualified to appear on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot.

Michigan’s official election calendar sets November 17, 2026 as the deadline for county canvassing boards to complete the November general-election canvass, and November 23 as the deadline for the Board of State Canvassers to meet to canvass the election.

Forecast: The endorsement may become a late-campaign test of whether Democrats can keep attention on turnout and economic issues; AP reported that El-Sayed and Michigan Democrats were trying to redirect attention toward Election Day mobilization.

story_report.summary: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan’s U.S. Senate race two days before the midterm election, breaking publicly with Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed after a feud over campaign advertising. The endorsement put Stevens on the opposite side of her party’s Senate nominee in the campaign’s final days, while Democrats and El-Sayed sought to direct attention toward Election Day mobilization and economic issues.

sections.heading: Stevens and El-Sayed Advertising Dispute
sections.body: ABC reported that Stevens said El-Sayed told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign, an exclusion she cited when announcing her support for Rogers. Their public dispute centered on a grocery-price advertisement that Stevens described as antisemitic and urged El-Sayed to condemn. The ad was produced by Rebellion PAC rather than El-Sayed’s campaign; the campaign said it was unaffiliated with the ad, and El-Sayed said he did not agree with its contents.

sections.heading: Michigan Election Certification Timeline
sections.body: Michigan’s Board of State Canvassers certified the August primary nominees for the Nov. 3, 2026 general-election ballot. Under the state election calendar, county canvassing boards must complete their general-election canvass by Nov. 17, and the Board of State Canvassers must meet to canvass the election by Nov. 23. AP reported that El-Sayed and Michigan Democrats were trying to refocus the closing campaign on turnout and economic issues.

unresolved.text: Reporting establishes the public dispute and the campaign’s request that Stevens not participate, but does not independently establish whether additional private negotiations contributed to her final decision to endorse Rogers.
The endorsement’s effect on the vote will remain uncertain until returns are reported and the statutory canvass is completed.

related_stories.title: Trump Administration Appeals to Supreme Court Over California Ballots
related_stories.summary: The Trump administration has filed an emergency application with the Supreme Court, seeking to block the counting of 20,000 mail-in ballots in California. The administration claims these ballots may belong to non-U.S. citizens, a claim that has been rejected by multiple courts and independent analyses. California officials warn that such a move could disenfranchise eligible voters.

related_stories.title: Charges Dismissed Against Former FBI Officials in Hunter Biden Investigation
related_stories.summary: A federal judge has dismissed charges against two former FBI officials, Nicole Floris and Bradley Benavides, who were accused of lying to Congress regarding their knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigation. The judge expressed concerns about the handling of the case, citing issues of 'weaponization' within the Justice Department. Although the charges were dismissed, the Justice Department may still pursue a grand jury indictment against the officials.

related_stories.title: Trump Urges Republican Unity Ahead of Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: In a final campaign push at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, President Donald Trump emphasized the importance of the upcoming midterm elections, calling them 'the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime.' He acknowledged the historical challenges faced by the president's party in midterms but urged Republicans to unite and vote. Trump's remarks come as he campaigns alongside other candidates in a bid to bolster Republican turnout.
